title: Honest Interval Length for Surrogate-Assisted ATE with Rare Surrogate-Outcome Discordance
banked_reason: The marked audit mechanism breaks signed pooling, but the verified result is an elementary compression obstruction. No defensible field-level precision frontier was found beyond the prohibited inherited kernels.

Its displayed proportional subfamily does not realize the claimed pooled mean: with lambda_10=lambda_01=L u/U(p,L), mu_10+mu_01=L(1+d(p))u/[2U(p,L)]=[(1+d(p))/(1-d(p))]u, not u except at d(p)=0; thus the stated pooling route is false and load-bearing.
Reject this duplicate and algebraically invalid core; pivot to a genuinely non-aggregable rare-validation problem rather than revising the inherited selector.

proof_attempt_summary: The presolve contained exact finite-cell likelihood calculations and an original-model rational interval upper certificate. The bounded root-changing retry verified a concrete marked finite-row law, twelve exact finite-cell checks, and an explicit non-aggregation pair. Independent 128-bit replay verified the inherited original-model rational upper certificate over 6561 grid constraints (coverage >=0.9016, length <=6.337333334). These do not prove marked-design minimax precision or attainability. The original signed-pooling subfamily is algebraically false; the main Gaussian-Poisson/interval/selector/global-minimax kernels are repo-subsumed. No Lean formalization began, no substrate build was requested, and no field-level theorem was established.
tldr: Primary binary outcomes can be expensive even when a cheap binary surrogate predicts them almost perfectly. When the validated sample has finitely many expected discrepancies and the independent cheap sample has order \(n^2\) records, both composition noise and primary-outcome correction contribute at scale \(n^{-1}\). The proposed result characterizes the all-rule \(90\%\)-honest connected-interval expected-length value, certifies it with finite whole-interval programs, and transfers it to one exactly honest original-data interval with unknown composition. The Gaussian-four-Poisson experiment and signed-count pooling are credited supporting reductions. A replayed positive-envelope certificate supports a strict gain over the stated fixed Gaussian bias interval; the global observable transfer remains the main open question.
gap: Kallus and Mao establish surrogate-assisted fixed conditional-law ATE efficiency, while generic confidence-set decision theory and the internal adjudication predecessor leave scale-preserving unknown-composition original-data attainment unresolved.
fill: The kernel matches an all-rule original-data minimax value to the supremum of local connected values and constructs an observed-data attaining sequence through a composition-indexed certified library and a uniformly short honesty repair.
